levels.name: Foundations
levels.focus: Classes, objects, encapsulation, composition over inheritance, clean interfaces, enums, basic validation. Model the nouns and verbs correctly before reaching for patterns.
levels.exit: You can turn a vague prompt into entities, relationships and a working in-memory implementation in 45 minutes, with no god classes.

levels.name: Design Patterns
levels.focus: Recognise when a problem is really a State, Strategy, Observer, Chain of Responsibility, Decorator, Composite, Factory or Builder problem, and apply the pattern without over-engineering.
levels.exit: You pick a pattern because a requirement forces it, and you can name the requirement that would make you remove it.

levels.name: Real-World Systems
levels.focus: Multi-actor business domains with workflows, pricing, search, and the first taste of concurrency (seat locking, double booking). Layering: domain, service, repository.
levels.exit: You separate domain model from services and storage, handle concurrent writes to shared resources, and keep the design open for the obvious next feature.

levels.name: Concurrency & Infrastructure Components
levels.focus: Build the components other systems sit on: rate limiters, thread pools, brokers, caches, pools, circuit breakers. Thread safety, back-pressure and failure handling become primary requirements.
levels.exit: You can argue the correctness of your locking strategy, explain memory/time complexity, and show how the component degrades under load.

levels.name: Staff-Level Domains
levels.focus: Money, matching engines, rule engines and workflows where correctness is non-negotiable. Idempotency, auditability, ledgers, versioning and extensibility by configuration rather than code changes.
levels.exit: Your design survives retries, partial failures and new business rules without a rewrite, and you can defend every invariant.

levels.name: Principal-Level Frameworks
levels.focus: Design the frameworks and platforms other teams build on: DI containers, saga orchestrators, policy engines, event sourcing, middleware pipelines. API ergonomics, backward compatibility, multi-tenancy and evolution over years.
levels.exit: You design for other engineers as users: stable contracts, extension points, migration paths, and clear failure semantics.

problems.title: Parking Lot
problems.statement: Design the software for a multi-floor parking lot. Vehicles of different sizes enter through entry gates, are assigned a compatible free spot, receive a ticket, and pay on exit based on time parked. Operators need to see live availability per floor and spot type. The lot should be able to add new vehicle types, spot types and pricing schemes without rewriting the core.
fr: Support multiple floors, each with spots of types Compact, Regular, Large and EV-charging
Support vehicle types Motorcycle, Car, Van/Truck, with a defined compatibility matrix (e.g. a car fits Regular or Large)
Issue a ticket on entry with ticket id, spot, vehicle number and entry time
Allocate the nearest compatible free spot using a pluggable allocation strategy
Compute fee on exit using a pluggable pricing strategy (hourly, flat first-hour, weekend rates)
Accept payment (cash, card, UPI) and free the spot once paid
Show live free-spot counts per floor and per spot type on a display board
Reject entry with a clear reason when the lot is full for that vehicle type
nfr: Spot allocation must be O(log n) or better per request
Two entry gates must never assign the same spot (thread-safe allocation)
Adding a new vehicle or spot type should not modify existing allocation code (OCP)
Core logic must be unit-testable with an injected clock
constraints: Up to 10 floors, 500 spots per floor
Up to 5 entry and 5 exit gates operating concurrently
In-memory storage is acceptable; persistence behind an interface
Fees in INR, rounded up to the next started hour by default
edge: Vehicle tries to exit with a lost or invalid ticket
Same vehicle number tries to enter twice
Payment fails after the fee is computed
A spot goes out of service while occupied
Two gates request the last free spot at the same instant
Vehicle parks for under one minute or across midnight / multiple days
behavior: park(vehicle) returns a Ticket or throws LotFullException(vehicleType)
unpark(ticketId, payment) returns a Receipt with duration, fee and payment status; spot becomes free only after successful payment
displayBoard.snapshot() returns counts per floor × spot type that reflect every completed park/unpark
followups: Add reservations made in advance from a mobile app
Support EV charging billed per kWh in addition to parking time
Make it work across 50 lots in a city with a central dashboard
clar: Yes, multiple floors; each floor has a mix of spot types.
Hourly by vehicle type; first hour flat. Assume pricing rules will change often.
Not in scope for v1, but don't make it impossible.
Nearest to the entry gate by default; the business may want other strategies later.
Model a Payment abstraction; actual gateway integration is out of scope.

problems.title: Tic-Tac-Toe (N×N)
problems.statement: Design a Tic-Tac-Toe game engine that works on an N×N board for two or more players. The engine validates moves, detects wins and draws efficiently, and supports both human and bot players. It should be easy to plug in a new win rule or a new player type.
fr: Create a game with board size N (N ≥ 3) and K players with unique symbols
Players take turns in a fixed order; reject moves out of turn
Validate a move: inside the board, cell empty, game not over
Detect a winner after each move (full row, column or either diagonal)
Detect a draw when the board is full with no winner
Support human players and bot players behind one Player interface
Support undo of the last move
nfr: Win detection in O(1) per move, not O(N²)
Engine independent of any UI (console, web, API)
constraints: Single process, single game per engine instance
edge: Move after the game has ended
Undo when no moves were made
behavior: makeMove(player, row, col) returns GameState IN_PROGRESS, WON(player) or DRAW
Invalid moves throw InvalidMoveException with a reason and do not advance the turn
undo() restores the previous board, the turn and the win counters
concepts: Separation of game logic and IO
O(1) win check using row/col/diagonal counters
followups: Win condition becomes K-in-a-row instead of full row
Add spectators who get notified on each move
clar: No, N×N where N is configurable.
Two by default but design for more.
No UI; expose an engine API. A console driver is enough to demo.
Yes, at least a random bot; smarter bots later.

problems.title: Snake and Ladder
problems.statement: Design a Snake and Ladder game supporting multiple players, a configurable board with snakes and ladders, and configurable dice. Players roll in turn, move, and are moved by snakes or ladders; the first to reach the last cell exactly wins. The rules vary between families, so rules must be pluggable.
fr: Board of configurable size (default 100) with configurable snakes (head → tail) and ladders (start → end)
Validate board config: no cycles, no snake/ladder on start or end cell, no cell with two jumps
One or more dice; configurable faces
Players move in round-robin; first to land exactly on the last cell wins
Support rule variants: extra turn on six, three sixes cancels, overshoot bounce-back
Game continues for remaining players to rank 2nd, 3rd, etc. (optional mode)
nfr: Deterministic tests via an injectable dice
New rule variants added without editing the game loop
edge: Roll that overshoots the final cell
Snake tail landing on a ladder start (chains)
Invalid board with snake head on cell 100
behavior: play() returns ranking of players
Each turn emits a TurnResult with roll, from, to and any jump taken
clar: Yes by default, but some variants allow overshoot.

problems.title: Library Management System
problems.statement: Design a system for a public library to manage its catalogue, members, borrowing, returns, reservations and fines. A title can have many physical copies. Members borrow copies, can reserve titles that are all checked out, and are fined for late returns. Librarians manage the catalogue.
fr: Catalogue of books (title, authors, ISBN, subject) with multiple BookItems (copies) each with a barcode and status
Search by title, author, subject or ISBN
Members borrow up to a limit of copies for a fixed period
Return a copy; compute fine for overdue days
Reserve a title when no copy is available; notify the first reserver when a copy returns
Renew a loan if no one has reserved the title
Librarians add/remove books and block members
nfr: Search response under 200 ms for 1M items (indexing)
Fine policy configurable per membership type
constraints: Max 5 active loans per member, 14-day loan by default
edge: Member with unpaid fines tries to borrow
Returning a copy that was reserved by someone else
Reserved copy not collected within 3 days
Renewal requested on an overdue loan
behavior: checkout(memberId, barcode) returns Loan or a typed error (LimitReached, HasFines, Reserved, NotAvailable)
return(barcode) returns Fine (possibly zero) and triggers reservation notification
clar: Yes, each copy is tracked separately.
Yes, a FIFO queue per title.
Per day overdue, policy differs by membership type.

problems.title: Shopping Cart & Checkout
problems.statement: Design the cart and checkout module of an e-commerce store. Customers add products with variants to a cart, apply coupons, see a price breakdown with taxes and shipping, and check out into an order. Discounts and tax rules change frequently and must be pluggable.
fr: Add, update quantity, remove line items (product + variant)
Validate stock at add time and again at checkout
Apply coupons: percentage, flat, buy-X-get-Y, free shipping; define stacking rules
Compute subtotal, discounts, tax (GST by category), shipping and grand total
Persist cart for guests and merge into user cart on login
Checkout creates an Order with a snapshot of prices; cart is cleared
nfr: Money must use fixed-point/decimal, never floats
Price computation deterministic and explainable (line-level breakdown)
New discount type added without touching existing ones
edge: Price changes between add-to-cart and checkout
Item goes out of stock during checkout
Guest cart merge with duplicate items
behavior: cart.summary() returns line items, each discount applied with reason, taxes and totals
checkout() returns Order or a list of validation problems the UI can display
clar: Percentage, flat, BOGO, free shipping. More will come.
At most two, and only one percentage coupon.
GST rate depends on product category.

problems.title: Employee Directory & Org Chart
problems.statement: Design an employee directory that models an organisation's reporting hierarchy, departments and roles. HR can add, move and remove employees; anyone can query reporting chains, direct reports, headcount per department and the lowest common manager of two employees.

Move an employee (and optionally their subtree) to a new manager

Lowest common manager of two employees

edge: Moving a manager under their own report (cycle)
behavior: move() rejects cycles with a clear error
queries reflect writes immediately

problems.title: Snake Game
problems.statement: Design the engine for the classic Snake game on a W×H grid. The snake moves one cell per tick in its current direction, grows when it eats food, and dies on hitting a wall or itself. Food appears at random free cells. The engine must be UI-agnostic and deterministic under test.
fr: Grid of configurable width and height
Snake moves one cell per tick; direction changes via input
Eating food grows the snake by one and increases score
Food spawns on a random free cell
Game over on wall or self collision
Optional wrap-around mode instead of walls
nfr: Each tick O(1) (deque body + occupied-cell set)
edge: Moving into the cell the tail is leaving this tick
No free cell left for food (win)
behavior: tick() returns TickResult: MOVED, ATE, GAME_OVER(reason)
changeDirection ignores direct reversal
clar: Walls by default; wrap is a mode.
What if the snake fills the board?

problems.title: Minesweeper
problems.statement: Design a Minesweeper engine: a board with hidden mines, numbered cells, reveal and flag actions, flood-fill reveal of empty regions, and win/lose detection. The first click must never be a mine.
fr: Mines placed after the first click, excluding that cell (and optionally its neighbours)
reveal(r,c): mine loses; number shows count; zero flood-fills
Chord: reveal neighbours when flag count matches number
Win when all non-mine cells revealed
nfr: Flood fill iterative (no stack overflow on large boards)
behavior: reveal returns the list of cells newly revealed and game state

problems.statement: Design a university course registration system. Students register for course sections each term subject to prerequisites, seat limits, schedule clashes and credit limits. Full sections offer a waitlist. Admins manage courses and sections.

problems.title: URL Shortener (Object Model)
problems.statement: Design the object model and core logic of a URL shortener: create short codes for long URLs, custom aliases, expiry, redirect lookup and click analytics. Focus on the class design and code generation strategy, not distributed storage.

problems.title: Vending Machine
problems.statement: Design the controller software of a vending machine. A user selects a product, inserts money (coins, notes or card), receives the product and correct change, or cancels and gets a refund. The machine behaves differently depending on its current state, and an operator can restock products and collect cash.
fr: Inventory of products in slots with price and quantity
States: Idle, HasSelection, AcceptingMoney, Dispensing, OutOfService
Accept coins and notes of fixed denominations; card payments
Dispense product and return change using available denominations
Cancel at any time before dispensing returns all inserted money
Operator mode: restock, set price, collect cash, view sales
nfr: Invalid actions in a state are rejected, never crash
State logic extensible without long if/else chains
Never lose track of money: inserted = dispensed + returned + kept
behavior: Every action returns the new state and any output (product, change, error)
If change cannot be made, the transaction is refused before money is accepted or the money is refunded
followups: Multiple machines with a central server

problems.title: ATM System
problems.statement: Design the software running inside an ATM. A customer inserts a card, enters a PIN, chooses an operation (withdraw, deposit, balance, mini statement, PIN change), and the ATM talks to the bank's backend. Cash is dispensed from cassettes of different denominations. Failure in the middle of a withdrawal must not lose the customer's money.
fr: Card read and PIN validation with 3 attempts before card retention
Withdraw: check balance via bank, dispense using available notes, debit account
Session timeout and cancel at any step
nfr: Withdrawal must be atomic: debit reversed if dispense fails
All bank calls idempotent with a transaction id
constraints: Network to bank may be slow or down
edge: Amount not dispensable with current notes
behavior: State transitions: Idle → CardInserted → Authenticated → Transaction → Idle
Dispense uses Chain of Responsibility from highest note down
clar: Withdraw, deposit, balance, mini statement, PIN change.
What if the network fails after debit?
The debit must be reversed; design for it.

problems.title: Logging Framework
problems.statement: Design a logging library (like log4j or winston) that application code uses to log messages at levels, routed to one or more destinations (console, file, remote) with configurable formats. Logging must not slow down the application noticeably.

Structured context (request id, user id) attached to every log in a scope

Async mode: shutdown flushes pending messages
